title: Breakfast Casserole With Italian Sausage And Fontina Recipe
description: To get a flavorful casserole with a crisp top and a soft, custardy inside, here’s what you need to know: Even when left out in the oven overnight, white bread soaked up too much custard and turned to mush. Toasted Italian bread greatly improved the texture. Using whole milk instead of half-and-half or cream kept the casserole light and fluffy; incorporating a minimal amount ensured the dish remained firm. You want enough cheese and sausage to flavor the dish, but not so much that you are left with a greasy, soggy mess. Some recipes tasted contained pockets where certain ingredients tended to congregate; stagger the bread, sausage, and cheese mixtures in multiple layers. Building the casserole with care helped ensure every bite had flavor. To guarantee the custard soaked in evenly, cover the prepared casserole with plastic wrap and weigh it down for up to 24 hours.
ingredients: 1 pound hot or sweet Italian sausage , casings removed
1 tablespoon Frank’s Red Hot sauce (or half as much Tobasco)
directions: Adjust oven racks to upper-middle and lower-middle positions and heat oven to 400 degrees. Slice bread in half lengthwise, then slice each half crosswise into ½-inch-thick pieces. Spread bread in single layers on 2 rimmed baking sheets and bake until golden, 15 to 20 minutes, flipping bread and switching and rotating sheets halfway through. Let cool 15 minutes.

Cook sausage in large skillet over medium heat until no longer pink, about 5 minutes. Add onion and cook until golden, about 5 minutes. Remove from heat and add 1/4 cup chopped fresh basil to sausage mixture.

Grease 13- by 9-inch baking dish. Shingle half of bread in prepared pan so that edges overlap slightly. Top with half of sausage mixture and 1 cup cheese. Repeat with remaining bread, remaining sausage mixture, and remaining cheese.
Whisk eggs, milk, salt, pepper, and hot sauce in large bowl. Pour evenly over casserole. Wrap casserole with plastic and weigh it down. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour and up to 24.

Adjust oven rack to middle position and heat oven to 350 degrees. Let casserole stand at room temperature while oven is heating. Remove weights, unwrap casserole, and bake until the edges and center have puffed and top is golden brown, about 1 hour. Let cool 10 minutes. Serve.
